title: Dustyhorn death a 'suicide by cop,' jury suggests
article: A coroner's jury has ruled the death of a Saskatoon man shot by police in 2007 was a suicide - a ruling that suggests a "suicide by cop" situation.
Dwayne Dustyhorn was struck by five bullets and died at an apartment at 1209 Cumberland Ave. S. on Dec. 22, 2007, the inquest was told earlier this week.
Dustyhorn, 38, had been charged with assaulting his partner, Lori Worm, and was worried about going to jail, the inquest was told. The two had been drinking and arguing.
According to Worm, Dustyhorn called 911, although she said she warned him police would shoot him.
He taped two knives to his hands, she said, and when police arrived, there was a violent confrontation.

Police witnesses told the inquest that Dustyhorn rushed at them from inside the apartment. The inquest was told the man was not slowed by a closed door, throwing himself against it and tearing it from its hinges.
After Dustyhorn rushed at them a second time, police started shooting, and he died at the scene.
The jury is allowed to make recommendations aimed at preventing deaths in similar cases in future, but didn't in this case.
In a brief report to the coroner, the six-person jury ruled the Dustyhorn's death was caused by a "gunshot wound to the left upper chest."
The jury said it was a "suicide" - although it did not say Dustyhorn shot himself.
All the evidence presented at the inquest said it was the police who fired the gunshot that killed him. Dustyhorn was armed with knives but no gun, the inquest heard.
"Suicide by cop" is a phrase commonly used to describe situations where someone provokes a conflict with the police in the expectation they will use lethal force.
